front: Critical region for a discrete test
back: Lower: largest c with P(X ≤ c) ≤ α. Upper: smallest c with P(X ≥ c) ≤ α. Two-tailed: α/2 in each tail.
The probability of the critical region when H₀ is true; for discrete tests usually below the nominal level.
$H_0: \lambda = \lambda_0$; scale $\lambda$ to the period observed; find the tail probability of the observed count.

front: Normal approximation in a binomial test
back: If $np > 5$ and $nq > 5$: $X \approx \mathrm{N}(np, npq)$ with a continuity correction (e.g. $X \ge 40 \to Y > 39.5$).

front: Normal approximation in a Poisson test (Cambridge)

back: The tail in the direction of H₁, including the observed value: P(X ≥ x) for '>', P(X ≤ x) for '<'.
Fixed number of independent trials, two outcomes, constant probability of success.
Compare each tail probability with half the significance level (0.025 for a 5% test).
